article_title: Critical Gitea Flaw Lets a Self-Registered Account Turn a Git Patch Into Remote Code Execution

content_preview.title: Critical Gitea Flaw Lets a Self-Registered Account Turn a Git Patch Into Remote Code Execution
content_preview.summary: A critical Gitea vulnerability lets a repository writer convert a crafted patch into a live Git hook and run shell commands as the service account.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Gitea, the self-hosted Git platform, has patched a critical remote code execution vulnerability that lets anyone with ordinary repository write access run arbitrary shell commands as the server's own service account, according to a [GitHub security advisory](https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/security/advisories/GHSA-rcr6-4jqh-j84m). Because Gitea enables open registration by default, an outside visitor can obtain that write access simply by signing up and creating a repository, then...

editor_notes.content_quality: Clear, well-structured News piece (Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis) at 680 words, within the 400-1200 News range. Neutral, technical tone throughout with no sensationalism or AI self-reference.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 3 sources read from local gzip snapshots (source-0.html.gz = GitHub Security Advisory GHSA-rcr6-4jqh-j84m, source-1.html.gz = Gitea v1.27.1 release notes, source-2.html.gz = The Hacker News). Every specific claim checked against the raw decompressed HTML text, not re-fetched live: CVE-2026-60004, CVSS 9.8 and full vector string CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H, CWE-94, affected range >=1.17 <1.27.1 (article says 'through 1.27.0', consistent), vulnerable file services/repository/files/patch.go, the exact git apply --cached invocation, the add/add collision mechanism, the hooks/post-index-change hook path, the hook-return-value-not-propagated detail, the exploit prerequisites (Git 2.32+, enabled diffpatch route, writable+executable temp filesystem), the full exposure list (app.ini/secrets, env vars, mounted repos, DB credentials, OAuth credentials, other services), reporter credit 'NightRang3r', and advisory publish timestamp (datetime attribute 2026-07-28T17:34:46Z, matching 'July 28, 2026' and 'one day after' the release). Release notes snapshot confirms the article's central analytical point verbatim: the SECURITY section only lists 'fix(oauth2): enforce mandatory 2FA policy on OAuth2 authorize/grant endpoints', while the diffpatch fix appears solely under MISC as 'refactor: git patch apply' -- exactly as the article states. The Hacker News snapshot confirms the 'Gitea Cloud instances would be upgraded automatically' / 'Disabling open registration' mitigation language and the 'does not say the flaw has been exploited in the wild' framing nearly verbatim. No misattributions, no hallucinated quotes, no suspicious_patterns flagged in the manifest (all three null).
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every number, path, and quoted mechanism in the body traces directly to one of the three cited sources; no unsupported specifics found.
